correctness.rationale: Cauchy/Radon averaging converts the mean central section area into (1/2)int_K |x|^(−1)dx. Applying div(x/|x|)=2/|x| on K without an epsilon ball yields the exact boundary formula (1/4)int_(∂K)(x·normal)/|x|dS; puncture flux vanishes. For any tangential polyhedron of F identical regular p-gon faces at inradius h and face apothem a=1/(2 tan(pi/p)), the polar regular-face integral is 2p(int_0^(pi/p) sqrt(h^2+a^2 sec^2(t))dt−h*pi/p). Differentiating the provided elementary asinh/atan antiderivative gives the stated I(h,a,c). Substitution with standard unit-edge inradii and volume F p a h/6 yields all five constants. I independently recomputed these at 60-digit precision: normalized values 1.141337004996962, 1.190038681989777, 1.193401870299981, 1.205386007375507, 1.206448277260306, agreeing with separated supplied certified brackets. The original interval code was inspected; random-plane simulation is only corroboration, while strict separation follows from the analytic formula plus bounded interval evaluation.

originality.rationale: The fundamental spherical Radon and boundary-potential identities are classical and explicitly NOT new. Koldobsky 2013 gives central-section Radon machinery rather than an exact five-Platonic unit-edge table or ordering. Published SCOPE nearby records for icosahedral section polygon types, five-solid shadow-area variance and mean-square widths concern different functionals; they do not imply central-sectional mean area. A historical stereology table or direct substitution from an older general tangential-polyhedron potential formula could cover the precise constants; no such table was identified. This is a narrow best-of-knowledge originality pass for the five explicit values and dimensionless ranking, not the general integral formula.
residual_risks: Obscure classic stereology/convex-geometry tables may already contain some or all five mean central-section areas.
A generic closed regular-polygon face potential formula could make the explicit five values mechanically covered rather than independently original.

value.rationale: The five Platonic solids form a canonical complete family. Their expected through-center section areas are natural shape invariants, distinct from projection areas; exact, scale-free values and a strict order can be used as geometric benchmark data. Near-adjacent inequalities (cube/oct and dodec/ico) require controlled comparison, providing a mathematically motivated complete finite classification rather than an arbitrary sample of polyhedra.
